transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orbit CTO), Claire Wong (Orbit SRE), Marcus Lee (Orbit Product)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, request logs, and debugging flows. Customer wants to understand how Redwood surfaces request-level traces, correlates errors to traces, exportability of logs, retention and RBAC/SSO, and what a PoC/benchmark would look like.

Topics covered:
- Console tracing UI and correlation with request logs
- Error analysis workflows (rate-limiting, model fallbacks, partial generations)
- Request log retention/export and redaction/KMS for PII
- Debugging flows: reproduce requests, download traces, attach to tickets
- PoC scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone welcome, I'm Jordan from Redwood, thanks for taking the time. Priya's gonna run through the console demo, we'll pause for Qs.
[00:00:10] Samir: Hey thanks, yeah real quick - high level we're evaluating inference providers for our chatbot infra, main constraints are latency SLAs sub-200ms P95, and strict data residency and encryption. We'll also need logs for audits.
[00:00:25] Jordan: Totally, that's exactly what Priya will show - tracing tied to request ids, and the request logs page with retention settings.
[00:00:30] Priya: ok jumping in to the console, pardon my screen - so first panel is the tracing view, you can see a timeline of requests, each trace has a request id, model variant, region, and the route.
[00:00:48] Claire: sorry can you zoom on the trace detail, that view looks similar to a distributed trace for a microservice.
[00:00:55] Priya: yeah it's inspired by that, we capture timing for queueing, KV cache hits, token generation, and network egress. there's also an error bucket on the right where we auto-group by error signature.
[00:01:14] Marcus: error signature meaning like model timeouts or decoding errors?
[00:01:18] Priya: exactly - timeouts, truncated outputs, invalid function calls, model fallback events (e.g., primary model overloaded and we routed to a cheaper variant). you can click a signature and see sample traces. note transcription may show the product name as "Redewood" sometimes in internal logs - small parsing oddity in earlier exports.
[00:01:40] Samir: hmm how do you tie a trace back to our system logs, we need to correlate a user id from our side.
[00:01:46] Priya: good question - request ids are generated by the Redwood SDK or API header you pass us (X-Request-ID). we keep that as an indexed tag, you can search by it. we also let you attach custom metadata/tags for tenancy or user ids.
[00:02:05] Marcus: and retention? We can't keep PII in third-party logs longer than 90 days for now.
[00:02:11] Priya: retention is configurable per workspace: default 90 days, short-term 7 days, or long-term 365 days for enterprise with add-on. we also support server-side redaction rules and KMS encrypted export for long-term storage.
[00:02:26] Claire: is the export format JSONL? we need to pipe into our SIEM.
[00:02:30] Priya: yep JSONL with schema versioning, includes trace span timing, token counts, model name, latency breakdown. we also include a hashed user id option so you can correlate without leaking raw PII.
[00:02:44] Samir: ok show me a debugging flow for a failing request.
[00:02:48] Priya: sure, here's an example trace where generation aborted at token 12, if I click into it you'll see spans: request received, queued, dispatched to GPU, generation start, model error, fallback to smaller model. there's a small stack with the raw request payload and console shows truncated user prompt to protect secrets.
[00:03:12] [00:03:12] Priya: we provide a "replay" feature - note this is a sandboxed replay that replays input against a pinned model version in a safe environment, it won't hit production data paths. that helps reproduce issues.
[00:03:29] Marcus: replay sounds great. Does replay run with the same batch behavior? We want to make sure it's faithful.
[00:03:35] Priya: by default it's single-request, but you can enable a batch-replay mode to simulate batching and concurrency; it will run with comparable kernel selection and quant profile if you use the same model config.
[00:03:48] Jordan: there's also an audit log that records who triggered a replay and what tag was used.
[00:03:55] Claire: ok on auth - SSO, RBAC, audit - we need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[00:04:00] Jordan: yes SAML SSO plus SCIM, fine-grained RBAC with route-level permissions, and audit logs exported to your SIEM. we can show the admin panel in the console as well.
[00:04:12] Samir: encryption at rest - do you support customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[00:04:17] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS for both logs and model checkpoints in Private deployments; for hosted we offer a bring-your-own-key option integrated with cloud KMS. HSM options are available on the Dedicated contract.
[00:04:32] Marcus: what about telemetry overhead? Adding tracing shouldn't add too much latency.
[00:04:36] Priya: tracing spans are lightweight, header-level tags and token counts are recorded asynchronously for many metrics; the per-request critical path adds <1ms on average, but queue size and batching are the bigger factors.
[00:04:49] [00:04:49] Jordan: quick qualifier: what's your expected qps and typical prompt length?
[00:04:55] Samir: we're planning 300 qps steady across a set of routes with some spikes to 1k qps; average prompt length ~120 tokens, occasionally 1k tokens for long context retrievals.
[00:05:07] Priya: noted - we'll recommend a dedicated pool for the high throughput routes and a hosted fallback for non-critical workloads, and we can preconfigure KV cache and batching policies.
[00:05:20] Marcus: can you show how error grouping works and how to drill to root cause for increase in 5xx?
[00:05:24] Priya: yeah, here's the error analysis page: trend view with groupings by error signature, then you can click into a signature to get sample traces and a histogram of latency and model variants. you can filter by model, region, or route. here's an example where a spike in 5xx correlated with a new model rollout.
[00:05:45] Claire: that's useful - we want regression alerts tied to our eval set.
[00:05:49] Priya: Redwood Optimize integrates with eval sets; you can link prompt/test sets and get quality regression alerts when embeddings similarity drops or answer correctness falls. we can plumb that into alerting.
[00:06:02] Samir: on model rollouts - can you auto-fallback to a variant when the primary is above latency SLOs?
[00:06:07] Priya: yes smart routing policies - you can set latency and cost thresholds, and the system will route to a compatible variant or dedicated pool. fallbacks are recorded as events in the trace.
[00:06:20] [00:06:20] Marcus: what visibility do we get into batching behavior that affects latency distribution?
[00:06:24] Priya: we expose batching heatmaps and per-route token distribution. you can see batch sizes over time and correlate with P50/P95 latency. there's also a suggestion engine in Optimize recommending batch windows and cache TTLs to reduce unit cost while meeting SLOs.
[00:06:40] Samir: sounds good. For PoC we want to run a 2-week benchmark with 300-1k qps and measure P50/P95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:06:49] Jordan: we'll include a benchmark plan in the follow-up - Priya can run a sample trace export from our demo workspace so you can see real output structure.
[00:06:58] Claire: quick security question - do you keep entire request payloads in logs by default? we need to avoid storing PII.
[00:07:04] Priya: by default we keep redacted payloads; full payload retention requires opt-in and enterprise controls. we also provide automatic redaction rules and allow customers to pass us hashed identifiers only.
[00:07:17] Samir: ok what's the cost model for Dedicated vs hosted for this PoC?
[00:07:22] Jordan: hosted is usage-based per-token with request/embedding pricing; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit that gives predictable throughput and unit cost reductions. we'll send an estimate for your target qps.
[00:07:35] Marcus: can you show how request logs look when exported and how schema changes are handled?
[00:07:40] Priya: exported JSONL includes a schema version header, and we keep backward-compatible fields. when we add new fields we bump the schema version; we keep a change log.
[00:07:52] [00:07:52] Priya: showing sample export now - you'll see fields: timestamp, request_id, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, trace_spans (array), tags.
[00:08:07] Claire: you said trace_spans is an array - will that break our parsers in SIEM? we prefer flattened fields.
[00:08:12] Priya: we can provide a flattened export variant that normalizes the first N spans into top-level fields, or a transformer that writes to your SIEM via a connector.
[00:08:24] Samir: that's great. Any rate limits on exports? we'll be streaming a lot.
[00:08:28] Priya: we have export throughput tiers; for PoC we'll open a higher export window. exports can be pushed to S3 with lifecycle rules or streamed to your endpoint.
[00:08:42] Marcus: demo the tracing search by user id and by error signature.
[00:08:46] [00:08:46] Priya: search box takes free text: request id, user id, or tag. here's search by tag user:12345 - results show traces and linked request logs. clicking a trace shows full span timeline. you can add comments on trace for PR triage.
[00:09:05] Claire: do you keep the KV cache events? We need to know if a response was served from cache.
[00:09:10] Priya: yes we record KV cache hits as spans and annotate token savings and latency reduction. you can aggregate KV hit ratio per route.
[00:09:20] Samir: okay about network egress when using private deployment - can we restrict region and control egress?
[00:09:26] Jordan: yes Private gives you control plane in VPC, we support region pinning and no public egress if required. for hosted you can select region and we have egress controls but not full air-gapped.
[00:09:38] [00:09:38] Marcus: what's the typical time to onboard a Dedicated pool?
[00:09:42] Jordan: provisioning depends on capacity, typically 2-4 weeks for a standard Dedicated cluster, quicker if we have reserved slots; Private on-prem is longer.
[00:09:52] Samir: okay good. any caveats on replay fidelity when model uses KV cache?
[00:09:57] Priya: replay can simulate KV cache hits by replaying the cache state snapshot if you opt into that; otherwise cache hits won't be identical. we capture KV cache keys as hashes to avoid exposing data.
[00:10:11] Marcus: can we get synthetic load generation from Redwood for the PoC?
[00:10:15] Jordan: yes we can provide a load script and runbench harness; we'll coordinate on the exact prompt set.
[00:10:22] Samir: let's talk timeline - we'd like a PoC in two weeks, aim to start Nov 8 and run for two weeks.
[00:10:28] Jordan: sounds reasonable, we'll follow up after the call with dates.
[00:10:33] Claire: question about anomaly detection - how do you surface regressions that are not simple error spikes?
[00:10:39] Priya: Optimize has a drift-detection agent that watches embedding spaces and token distributions; when a model starts to drift against a baseline prompts set it raises alerts and links to traces where the responses diverged.
[00:10:55] Marcus: show me the request logs retention UI and redaction rule example.
[00:11:00] [00:11:00] Priya: opening logs settings - you can set per-route retention, toggle automatic redaction by regex, and configure export targets. here's a sample rule: redact email-like patterns in payloads. when you update rules we run them retroactively with a job that reprocesses stored logs (enterprise only).
[00:11:20] Samir: retroactive jobs - any SLA on reprocessing time?
[00:11:24] Priya: depends on dataset size, typically a few hours for under 100k requests; larger datasets may take longer. we'll provide an ETA in the reprocess job UI.
[00:11:36] Claire: for compliance we need immutable audit logs for some actions.
[00:11:40] Jordan: we have append-only audit logs with exportable digest and optional push to your SIEM.
[00:11:47] Marcus: ok the final bit - how do we triage a partial generation that returns garbage 30% of the time?
[00:11:53] Priya: you'd set up an alert for error signature frequency and link to samples; then you can replay failing inputs and try alternate model variants or quant profiles. we can also run a small A/B rollout to test fixes.
[00:12:10] Samir: excellent. any known gotchas with our stack - we use GCP us-central1 primarily and have a mix of k8s and serverless frontends.
[00:12:19] Priya: GCP is supported, region us-central has low latency from our hosted endpoints; if you need on-prem colocation we'd discuss Private. SDK integrates with k8s service mesh headers; serverless needs sticky headers for large context but we've seen customers successfully integrate.
[00:12:36] [00:12:36] Jordan: we should recap next steps real quick.
[00:12:40] Jordan: action items: Jordan send pricing & security docs, Priya share trace export and load script, Samir provide network constraints and sample dataset. Schedule PoC kickoff Nov 8.
[00:12:52] Marcus: ok thanks this was helpful.
[00:12:55] Samir: will you include a short doc on how to map our logs to Redwood trace fields?
[00:12:59] Priya: yes I'll include a mapping guide and an example SIEM connector config.
[00:13:06] [00:13:06] Jordan: sweet, we'll follow up via email with meeting notes.
[00:13:12] Claire: quick micro question - can replay be triggered via API, not just console?
[00:13:16] Priya: yes replay has an API endpoint for automation and we record the job id in the audit log.
[00:13:24] Samir: thanks folks.
[00:13:26] [00:13:26] End of main demo, remaining time used for deeper technical Qs and clarifications.

[00:13:30] [00:13:30] Technical deep-dive snippets (selected):
[00:13:30] Claire: show me an example trace payload.
[00:13:34] Priya: here's a sanitized JSON object - note internal fields sometimes get mis-transcribed in exports (eg "kv_cache" appears as "k v cache"), older export parsers had spacing issues.
[00:13:46] Marcus: odd but ok, we'll handle that in our parser.
[00:13:50] Priya: also, traces include token-by-token timing in a compact representation; we compress spans for long contexts.
[00:13:58] Samir: latency numbers - do you include GPU kernel times vs scheduling?
[00:14:03] Priya: yes separate spans for scheduling, kernel execution, and serialization. that helped one customer find a serialization bug in their payload encoding.
[00:14:16] Claire: about schema changes - do you version trace schema so our parsers don't break?
[00:14:20] Priya: yes schema versioning and changelog in the export. we'll also send a migration guide for any new fields.
[00:14:30] Marcus: final question - can Redwood redact based on user-supplied regex on ingest?
[00:14:35] Priya: yes you can supply regex or a custom sanitizer function in Private deployments; for hosted we provide standard regex rules and enterprise-facing custom rules.
[00:14:47] Samir: great ok that's all for questions.

[00:14:50] Jordan: thanks again everyone, expect the follow-up with PoC checklist, pricing, and security docs.
[00:14:56] Claire: thanks, bye.

End of meeting.
